You can change your card PIN in the app or at an ATM.

In the app:
1) Open Cards > Select your card > Change PIN (or Security > Change PIN).
2) Verify your identity (device biometrics, account password, or OTP).
3) Enter a new 4–6 digit PIN and confirm. Avoid obvious patterns like 0000, 1234, dates, or repeated digits.

At an ATM:
1) Insert your card and choose PIN Services (Change/Set PIN).
2) Authenticate (usually with your current PIN, sometimes with additional verification).

- Your card must be active and not expired.

- Use a unique PIN, avoid birthdays, addresses, or simple sequences.
- Don’t share or write down your PIN; cover the keypad at ATMs and POS.

- Option missing/greyed out: Update the app, check card status (active), and region support.
- OTP not received: Check signal and your bank’s registered contact details; retry after 5–10 minutes.
- Too many wrong attempts: Your card may lock after several failed tries. Wait the cooldown or contact Support to unlock.

Try these steps to restore contactless:

Basics
- Make sure the card is active and not expired. Clean the front of the card gently with a soft cloth and check for cracks, bends, or heat damage.
- Tap the card over the contactless symbol and hold still for 1–2 seconds. Move the card around the logo—antennas are not always centered.
- Remove the card from metal wallets/RFID sleeves and keep other NFC cards/phones away from the reader during the tap.

App and card settings
- Open Cards > Select your card and ensure it’s not frozen and contactless is enabled (if your app has a contactless toggle).
- If you recently changed your PIN or received a replacement card, perform one chip-and-PIN transaction (insert card) to activate/sync contactless.

Limits and resets
- Local contactless limits apply. For larger amounts or after several taps, terminals may require you to insert the card and enter your PIN—that’s normal and resets the contactless counter.
- Multiple wrong PIN attempts or risk checks may temporarily disable contactless. Do a chip-and-PIN transaction or wait for the cooldown, then try tapping again.

Merchant and terminal
- Not all terminals support contactless or may be offline. Try another terminal/merchant or ask the cashier to restart the reader.
- If traveling, ensure international usage is enabled with your issuer; some regions use offline/contactless rules that differ.

If it still fails
- Check the app for decline reasons (insufficient funds, card blocked, region restrictions). Unfreeze the card if needed.
- Try a different merchant/terminal. If contactless fails consistently while chip-and-PIN works, the card’s antenna may be damaged.
- Contact Support to investigate. We can help reset counters or reissue a card if the contactless chip is faulty. Please share the last 4 digits of your card, date/time of the attempts, merchant location, and any terminal message.

Common decline reasons and how to fix them:

1) Card status and basics
- Not activated or frozen: Open the app > Cards > Select your card, and make sure it’s activated and not frozen.
- Card replaced/expired: Use your latest card; expired or deactivated cards will decline.
- Damaged card: Bent, cracked, or heat-damaged chips/antennas can cause declines. Try chip-and-PIN on a different terminal or request a replacement.

2) Funds, limits, and holds
- Insufficient funds: Check your balance in the app. Some merchants place a preauthorization (e.g., hotels, rentals, fuel) that is higher than the final amount; ensure you have enough to cover the hold.
- Limits reached: You may have hit daily, per-transaction, ATM, or contactless counters. Insert the card and enter your PIN to reset contactless counters or wait for limits to refresh.

3) Authentication and data mismatches (online)
- Wrong PIN/CVV/expiry: Re-enter carefully.
- Address/ZIP mismatch (AVS): Update your billing address in the app to match what the merchant checks.
- 3D Secure/OTP not completed: Finish the verification step; if OTP wasn’t received, retry after checking your signal and registered contact details.

4) Merchant, category, and regional rules
- Unsupported merchant category (e.g., gambling/crypto): Transactions in restricted categories will be declined.
- International usage: If traveling or buying abroad, enable international usage with your issuer where required. Local rules and offline terminal behavior can differ.
- Terminal issues: Some terminals are offline or misconfigured. Try another terminal/merchant or ask the cashier to restart the reader.

5) Contactless specifics
- Exceeded contactless limits or risk checks: Insert the card and enter your PIN to reset; this is normal.
- Tap not detected or repeated declines: Remove the card from metal wallets/RFID sleeves and keep other NFC cards/phones away when tapping. If tap still fails while chip works, the antenna may be faulty.

What to do next
- Check the app timeline for the decline reason and card status.
- Verify balance, card activation, and billing address.
- Retry with chip-and-PIN (insert) and ensure the correct PIN.
- For online payments, complete any 3D Secure/OTP prompts and confirm CVV/address.
- If abroad, enable international usage and try another terminal.

Get help
If the payment continues to fail, contact Support. Share the last 4 digits of your card, date/time, merchant name/location/website, amount/currency, terminal message (e.g., Do Not Honor), and any screenshots/error codes. We’ll review the decline code, limits, and risk checks, and help resolve or reissue your card if needed.

Common reasons ATM cash withdrawals are declined and how to fix them:

1) Card status and PIN
- Not activated or frozen: Open the app > Cards > Select your card and make sure it’s activated and not frozen.
- Wrong PIN or too many attempts: Confirm your PIN. If you recently changed it, perform one chip‑and‑PIN transaction (ATM or POS) to sync the offline PIN. After multiple wrong tries, the card may temporarily lock—wait for the cooldown or contact Support.
- Card replaced/expired/damaged: Use your latest active card. Bent/cracked chips can cause declines; try a different ATM or request a replacement.

2) Funds, limits, and amounts
- Insufficient funds: Check your available balance in the app. Ensure enough to cover the withdrawal plus any ATM surcharge.
- Limits reached: You may have hit daily or per‑transaction ATM limits (or local network caps). Check Cards > Manage Limits in the app (if available) and try a smaller amount or wait until limits reset.
- Denominations and caps: Some ATMs only dispense set amounts (e.g., multiples of 10/20) or have low per‑transaction ceilings. Try adjusting the amount to match local denominations.

3) Network, region, and ATM compatibility
- ATM/network issues: The ATM may be offline or not connected to your card’s network. Try another ATM—preferably a major bank’s machine.
- International usage: When abroad, enable international usage with your issuer (if required). Regional rules and offline ATMs can differ and cause declines.
- Magstripe vs chip: Many ATMs require chip. If magstripe fallback is disabled on your card, a magstripe‑only ATM can decline. Use a chip‑capable ATM.

4) Card type and product rules
- Product restrictions: Some prepaid, virtual, or certain credit cards don’t allow cash withdrawals (cash advances). Check your card’s features in the app.
- Risk checks: Repeated declines or unusual activity can trigger protective blocks. Wait, try a different ATM, or contact Support.

What to do next
- In the app, check your card status, available balance, and ATM/cash limits. Look for any decline reason in the timeline.
- Retry with a smaller amount that matches local denominations, at a chip‑capable ATM from a major bank.
- Ensure the correct PIN and consider doing a chip‑and‑PIN transaction to sync the PIN if you recently changed it.
- If abroad, enable international usage and try another ATM/network.

If it still fails
- The ATM’s reader or network may be the issue; try a different location/bank.
- If POS purchases work but ATM withdrawals consistently fail, your card may not support cash withdrawals or may be restricted. Contact Support.

Contact Support

We’ll review the decline code, limits, and regional settings, and help resolve or advise on reissuing the card if needed.

answer.text:
Disposable virtual cards inherit your primary card’s account-level limits (daily/monthly spend, risk/velocity checks, regional restrictions). In addition, you can set per-card controls at creation for extra security.

What you can control per disposable card:
- Per-transaction cap: Set the maximum amount allowed for a single authorization.
- Total budget: Set the total spend allowed across all authorizations (for limited-use cards).
- Number of transactions: Choose single-use (one successful authorization) or limited-use (e.g., up to N authorizations).
- Expiry window: Define how long the card remains active (e.g., 10–30 minutes, 24 hours). After expiry, the card number is retired and further attempts are declined.
- Merchant lock: Optionally restrict to a specific merchant/domain or MCC so the card only works where you intend.
- Geography: Apply country/region restrictions consistent with your account settings.

Defaults and restrictions:
- Disposable cards are intended for online use and do not support ATM withdrawals. In-store/contactless usage is typically not supported unless specifically enabled via a tokenized wallet.
- They share your account’s available balance and cannot exceed it. If your available funds or account limits are reached, authorizations are declined.
- Subscriptions and recurring payments are not recommended for single-use cards; use your primary card or a dedicated limited-use card with appropriate limits.
- Preauthorizations (e.g., hotels, rentals, fuel) may place a hold higher than the final amount. Set the per-transaction cap to cover potential holds if you intend to use a disposable card for such merchants.

Settlements, refunds, and retries:
- If a merchant completes a capture for an approved authorization, it will settle normally even if the disposable card has expired after the initial approval.
- Refunds for transactions made with a disposable card are credited back to your underlying account, even if the card number is retired.
- New authorization attempts after expiry or beyond the configured limits will be declined.

Security and compliance:
- AVS (billing address), CVV, and 3D Secure/OTP checks apply the same way as your primary card. Mismatches or failed challenges can cause declines.
- Merchant category and regional blocks carry over to disposable cards.

Troubleshooting declines:
- Limit exceeded or expired: Increase the per-transaction cap/total budget or recreate the card with a longer expiry.
- Merchant mismatch: Ensure the card isn’t locked to a different domain/MCC.
- Insufficient funds or account limits: Check available balance and daily/monthly limits in the app.
- International usage: Enable/allow usage in the destination country if required.

How to manage:
- Create and configure limits in the app: Cards > Disposable Cards > Create.
- View, pause, or delete a disposable card under Cards > Disposable Cards. For recurring or higher-risk merchants, consider using a limited-use card with a tight per-transaction cap and merchant lock.

Tip: Use a fresh disposable card per merchant and purchase for maximum protection, and set the expiry window short (e.g., 30 minutes) with a per-transaction cap that matches the expected charge.

Overview
- Foreign currency transactions are converted at the card network’s exchange rate (e.g., Visa/Mastercard) plus our transparent FX fee. Typical FX fees range from 0.5% to 2%, depending on the currency, region, and transaction amount. Major currencies (USD, EUR, GBP) generally have lower fees; less‑common currencies may be higher.

Rate source and timing
- Rate basis: We use the card network’s rate at authorization and/or at settlement. The final posted amount can differ slightly from the initial authorization if the network rate changes before settlement.
- Weekends/holidays: Markets and network adjustments can lead to slightly wider spreads or markups on weekends and public holidays.

Fee structure
- Percentage fee: Applied to the converted amount. Typical range: 0.5%–2%.
- No hidden charges: FX fees are shown in your transaction details. Any additional merchant or ATM surcharge will also be displayed when available.

Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC)
- At checkout or on an ATM abroad, you may be offered to pay in your home currency via the merchant’s conversion. This is usually more expensive.
- Tip: For the best rate, choose to pay in the local currency and decline DCC. Our FX fee and network rate are often more favorable than merchant conversions.

Special cases
- Preauthorizations (hotels, car rentals, fuel): The initial hold may be higher than the final amount. The final settlement uses the prevailing network rate; amounts can vary.
- Refunds: Refunded amounts convert back at the network rate on the refund date. Due to rate moves, the refund value in your home currency may differ from the original charge.
- ATM abroad: Cash withdrawals are converted similarly, but the ATM/operator may add a local surcharge or offer DCC. Choose local currency and decline DCC where possible.

How to check and minimize costs
- In‑app rate: You can view the current estimated rate and the FX fee in the app before or after a transaction.
- Choose local currency: Decline DCC at terminals and ATMs to avoid merchant markups.
- Watch timing: Settlement amounts can vary slightly from authorization due to rate changes.

Visibility and support
- Breakdown: Your transaction details show the original currency amount, converted amount, and any FX fee or surcharge when available.
- Help: If an FX total looks off, contact Support with the transaction date/time, merchant/ATM, original currency amount, posted amount, and any receipt showing DCC or surcharges. We’ll review the network rate, applied fee, and any merchant conversion.

- Taxes and service fees: VAT, sales tax, convenience/platform fees, shipping, or handling may be added at posting.
- Settlement differences: The posted amount can differ slightly from authorization due to exchange rate changes, rounding, partial captures, or split shipments.
- Small test charges: A $0/$1 temporary authorization may appear during card verification and is automatically reversed.

How to review in the app
- Open the transaction details to see: original amount, converted/home‑currency amount, any FX fee or ATM surcharge (when available), and whether the entry is a hold/pending or a posted charge.
- For foreign transactions, look for notes indicating DCC or local currency vs home currency.

If you don’t recognize the charge
- Check the merchant name (it may differ from the storefront), location/website, and time.
- Look for recent orders, subscriptions/trials, split shipments, or tips. Marketplaces can show platform names instead of the seller.
- If it still looks unfamiliar, use the Dispute option in the app. We’ll investigate and help reverse unauthorized charges when appropriate.

Tips to avoid extra costs
- Decline DCC and pay in local currency when abroad.
- Review ATM screens for surcharges and consider using bank ATMs with clearer fee disclosures.
- Expect holds at hotels, rentals, and fuel stations; these will be replaced by the final amount after settlement.

Contact Support
- If the extra amount seems incorrect or a hold hasn’t dropped within the merchant’s usual timeframe, contact Support. Include the transaction date/time, merchant/ATM name and location, receipt(s), any tip/service fee notes, and screenshots of the transaction details. We can provide a breakdown of the applied rate, fees, and settlement timeline, and assist with disputes where needed.

Create a disposable virtual card in the app to add extra protection for online purchases.

How to create
- Open Cards > Disposable Cards > Create (or Cards > Create Disposable Card).
- Set per‑card controls: per‑transaction cap, total budget (for limited‑use), allowed number of authorizations (single‑use or limited‑use), expiry window (e.g., 30 minutes, 24 hours), and optional merchant/domain (MCC/website) lock.
- Review the card details (number, expiry, CVV) and use them at checkout.

What to know
- Online‑first: Disposable cards are intended for online use and don’t support ATM withdrawals. In‑store/contactless is generally not supported unless explicitly enabled via a tokenized wallet (availability varies).
- Limits: Disposable cards inherit your account‑level limits (daily/monthly spend, risk/velocity checks, country/geography rules). They also share your available balance and cannot exceed it.
- Subscriptions/trials: Single‑use cards are best for one‑time purchases. For trials or short‑term subscriptions, use a limited‑use card with a tight per‑transaction cap, small total budget, and a short expiry. Ongoing subscriptions are better on your primary card with merchant controls.
- Preauthorizations: Some merchants (hotels, rentals, fuel) place higher holds than the final amount. If you must use a disposable card, set the per‑transaction cap high enough to cover the hold; otherwise the auth may be declined.

Refunds and retries
- Refunds for completed purchases credit back to your underlying account even if the disposable card has expired or been deleted.
- New authorization attempts after the card expires, exceeds its limits, or violates its merchant/geography lock will be declined.

Security
- The disposable card number is retired after expiry or once its usage limit is reached (for single‑use). Recreate a new card for future purchases.
- Standard checks (AVS, CVV, 3D Secure/OTP) apply and help prevent misuse.

Troubleshooting
- Declined: Increase the per‑transaction cap/total budget, confirm sufficient funds, and check that the card isn’t locked to a different merchant/domain or region.
- Card not showing or verification failed: Refresh the app, ensure your account is active and verified, and try creating the card again.

Tip
- For maximum protection, create a fresh disposable card per merchant and keep the expiry window short (e.g., 30 minutes) with a per‑transaction cap matching the expected charge. If you need to retry, you can quickly create a new card with adjusted limits.

Support
- If a payment fails, contact Support with the last 4 digits of the card, date/time, merchant website, amount/currency, and any error message or screenshot. We’ll review limits, risk checks, and merchant settings to help resolve.

Typical timelines
- Most pending authorizations finalize or drop within 1–3 business days.
- Some categories (hotels, car rentals, fuel stations, online marketplaces) commonly take longer—up to 7 days, and in certain cases up to 30 days depending on merchant processes and card network rules.

Holds and preauthorizations
- Hotels/car rentals: Often place a higher hold for incidentals or deposits. The hold is replaced by the final posted amount at checkout/return; any unused portion is released once the merchant finalizes.
- Fuel stations: May preauthorize a standard amount (e.g., higher than your fill). The final amount posts after the merchant submits the actual spend.
- Restaurants/bars: A base authorization may be adjusted later to include tips or service fees.

Why pending differs from posted
- Amount changes: Tips, partial captures, split shipments, taxes/fees, or merchant adjustments can make the posted amount differ.

- Rounding and batching: Minor differences can occur due to rounding or how the merchant batches settlements.

- Check details: Open the pending transaction in the app to see the merchant name, authorization amount, timestamp, and any notes.
- Don’t retry immediately: Avoid multiple retries that can create duplicate holds. If a payment appears stuck, ask the merchant to confirm whether the original authorization will be captured or voided.
- Contact the merchant: If the order was canceled or fulfilled differently, ask them to void the authorization or settle the correct amount.
- Wait for release: If the merchant doesn’t settle, the hold expires automatically per network rules and funds are released back to your available balance.

- Duplicate pendings: If you tried multiple times, you may see several holds. Unused authorizations will expire and drop automatically.
- Voids: A merchant can void an authorization; once processed, the pending entry should disappear (timing varies by network).
- Replacement/frozen card: Freezing or replacing a card does not force‑remove existing holds. Unused holds will still expire in their normal window.

Common causes (card top-ups)
- Insufficient funds: Your bank declined due to not enough balance or credit.
- Incorrect details: Card number, expiry, CVV, or billing address (AVS) mismatch.
- 3D Secure/OTP failed: Authentication timed out, was declined, or not completed.
- Card restrictions: Issuer blocks e‑commerce, cross‑border, or wallet loads; prepaid/virtual cards may be restricted.
- Expired/updated card: Old card on file no longer valid; try the new card.

Common causes (bank transfer top-ups)
- Incorrect beneficiary details: Account/IBAN, routing/BIC/SWIFT, or reference field wrong/missing.
- Name mismatch: Beneficiary name doesn’t match your account.
- Bank rejection/return: Sender bank or intermediary returned funds; compliance or sanctions screening.
- Cutoff/maintenance: Transfer initiated outside processing windows or during bank maintenance.

What to do (card top-ups)
- Verify details: Re‑enter card number, expiry, CVV, and correct billing address.
- Complete authentication: Accept 3D Secure/OTP promptly; disable VPN; ensure stable connection.
- Enable online payments: Ask your bank to enable e‑commerce and cross‑border transactions.
- Check funds/limits: Confirm available balance and try a smaller amount; review app limits.

  • Insufficient funds or issuer decline at settlement.

  • Name mismatch, sanctions/compliance screening, or bank maintenance.

What reversal looks like
- Card: A pending authorization may drop (no final charge), or a posted top‑up can show as a refund back to the original card.
- Bank: Incoming transfer status may change to Returned/Rejected; funds go back to the sender’s account.

Typical timelines
- Card authorization reversal: 24–72 hours to drop from your available balance; your bank may take a few days to reflect it.

- Bank transfer return: ACH/SEPA commonly 1–5 business days; SWIFT 2–10 business days (intermediary banks may add time).

How to check
- Open the transaction details in the app to see reversal/refund status, timestamps, and any notes (e.g., issuer declined, name mismatch, compliance review).
- For bank transfers, ask the sender for the transfer ID/reference and any return code their bank provided.

- Card top‑ups: Verify card details and billing address, complete 3D Secure/OTP promptly, ensure sufficient funds, and consider using a debit card (often fee‑free and higher acceptance). If your issuer flagged the transaction (cash advance/chargeback), contact your bank.
- Bank transfers: Confirm beneficiary name, account/IBAN, routing/BIC/SWIFT, and required reference exactly as shown in the app. Re‑send after correcting details. For cross‑border SWIFT, ask the bank to use appropriate fee options (SHA/OUR/BEN).

Fees and FX
- We do not charge a receiving fee for reversals. Third‑party bank or issuer fees are outside our control.
- Refund amounts can differ slightly due to exchange rate changes between the original top‑up and the reversal posting.

Preventing reversals
- Use the exact Account Details and required reference for bank transfers.
- Keep online payments and 3D Secure enabled on your card and avoid repeated rapid retries.
- Prefer local transfer rails (ACH/SEPA/Faster Payments) or debit card for smoother funding.

By transfer type

- SWIFT (International wires): May incur fees from intermediary/receiving banks. Depending on fee option (SHA/OUR/BEN), fees may be split or borne entirely by you or the recipient.

SWIFT fee options
- SHA (Shared): You pay our sending fee; the recipient may receive less due to intermediary/receiving bank fees.
- OUR (Sender pays all): You cover the sending and intermediary fees so the beneficiary receives the full amount (some banks still deduct unexpected fees outside our control).
- BEN (Beneficiary pays): The recipient pays all fees; the received amount will be reduced by intermediary/receiving fees.

FX and currency conversion
- If you send in a currency different from your balance or the beneficiary’s account, FX conversion applies. We display the live indicative rate and any FX fee before you confirm.
- Avoid DCC (dynamic currency conversion) where a merchant/bank converts at their rate; paying in local currency is generally more cost‑effective.

Expedited/priority transfers
- Choosing express/priority routes can speed posting but may add an extra fee. The app clearly shows any expedited charges before you send.

Visibility and receipts
- Before you confirm, you’ll see the transfer amount, estimated FX (if applicable), and our fee. For SWIFT, intermediary bank fees may not be fully itemized until after posting.

Refunds/returns
- If a transfer fails or is returned, our sending fee may be refunded depending on stage of processing. Third‑party fees (intermediary/receiving bank) are outside our control and may not be recoverable.

Tips to minimize fees
- Use local rails (ACH/SEPA/Faster Payments/RTP) instead of SWIFT when possible.

- For SWIFT, consider OUR if you want the recipient to receive the full amount (note: some intermediary banks may still deduct fees).

Overview

Card top‑ups commonly use Strong Customer Authentication (3D Secure/OTP), which may prompt an approval in your bank’s app or ask you to enter a one‑time code sent via SMS/email. In certain cases, compliance review (ID/selfie) may also be requested.

How to verify
1) Start your top‑up in the app and review the amount/fees.
2) When prompted, complete the bank approval (3D Secure) or enter the one‑time code sent via SMS/email.
3) If asked, confirm via your bank’s mobile app push or authenticator. Return to our app to finish.
4) Once verified, the top‑up posts instantly or within minutes.

Card vs bank transfers
- Card top‑ups: Usually require 3D Secure/SCA. Verification can be one‑time per card/device, but may be requested again based on issuer rules, risk checks, or unusual activity.
- Bank transfers: Do not use SMS codes from us. Verification may involve linking/confirming an external account (e.g., micro‑deposits) or compliance checks for large/unusual deposits.

Timing and codes
- OTP/code validity is short (typically a few minutes). If it expires, request a new code.
- You can usually resend after ~60 seconds. Ensure your device time is set to automatic.

Troubleshooting
- No code received: Check signal and email spam/junk, disable VPN/ad‑blockers, and ensure your registered phone/email is correct. Try the alternate channel (email vs SMS) or your bank’s app approval.
- 3D Secure timed out/failed: Use a stable internet connection, keep your bank app notifications enabled, and retry the flow. If the bank blocks e‑commerce or cross‑border loads, contact your issuer.
- 'Under review': Large or unusual deposits may need compliance verification. You’ll be notified when approved.

Fees and holds
- If verification fails, the top‑up won’t complete. Any temporary card authorization should reverse automatically per network rules (usually within 24–72 hours). We do not charge a processing fee on failed top‑ups.

Security
- We will never ask for your card PIN or passwords. Only enter one‑time codes in the verification screen.

About virtual cards
- Virtual cards are designed for online (card‑not‑present) purchases. Some merchants or categories do not accept virtual card numbers, require a physical card, or have extra checks that can cause declines.

Common reasons for declines
- Activation/balance: Ensure the virtual card is active, not frozen, and has sufficient available balance to cover the amount plus any preauthorization hold.
- Merchant acceptance: Certain MCCs (e.g., cash‑like transactions, high‑risk categories, some travel/services) may reject virtual cards or require a physical card. Contact the merchant to confirm they accept online card payments for your card brand.
- Details mismatch: Incorrect card number, expiry, CVV, name, or billing address (AVS) will be declined. Enter your billing address exactly as shown in the app.
- 3D Secure/SCA: Some merchants require OTP/app approval. If you missed or didn’t receive the prompt, the payment can fail. Retry with stable internet, notifications enabled, and no VPN/ad‑blockers.
- Country/issuer settings: Cross‑border e‑commerce may be blocked by your issuer or restricted by the merchant. If using a VPN or if IP location differs from billing country, the merchant may decline.
- Trial/recurring: $0/$1 test authorizations or recurring charges may fail if the merchant blocks virtual cards or requires a physical card token.
- Card type restrictions: Some issuers classify wallet loads, cash‑like transactions, or certain platforms as cash advances and may reject virtual cards.

What to try
- Verify card status and balance: In the app, check the virtual card is active and funded; remove any freeze.
- Re‑enter details: Carefully enter the card number, expiry, CVV, and the exact billing address/ZIP/postcode.
- Complete 3DS/OTP: Approve the bank’s verification promptly; keep notifications on and avoid VPN/proxy.
- Try a different channel: If the merchant’s website fails, try their official app or a different browser (no autofill).
- Contact the merchant: Ask if they accept your card brand for online payments and whether virtual cards are supported for subscriptions/recurring.
- Use a physical card or alternative method: If the merchant doesn’t accept virtual cards, use your physical card, a supported wallet, or bank transfer.

Special notes
- Apple Pay/Google Pay: Virtual card numbers may not be tokenized for in‑store tap; use your physical card for card‑present transactions.
- Holds and amount changes: Preauthorization amounts can differ from final capture (tips, deposits, adjustments). Ensure you have enough balance to cover potential increases.

Support
- If declines persist, contact Support with: date/time, merchant name/website/app, amount/currency, error/decline message or code, whether a 3D Secure prompt appeared, and screenshots. We’ll review issuer responses, merchant category, authentication, and any restrictions, and advise the best way to complete your purchase.

answer.text:
Identity verification (KYC) is required by financial regulations to prevent fraud, money laundering, and unauthorized access. It confirms you are the rightful account holder and enables secure financial services.

Why we verify
- Regulatory compliance: Laws require Know Your Customer (KYC), Anti‑Money Laundering (AML), and Counter‑Terrorist Financing (CFT) checks, plus sanctions/PEP screening.
- Security: Verifying your ID and selfie (liveness) protects against account takeover and helps recover your account if you lose access.
- Eligibility: Confirms age, residency, and that your details match your profile and payment methods.
- Risk management: Reduces fraud, chargebacks, and misuse, keeping fees and service quality stable for everyone.

When verification is needed
- Before enabling core features like sending/receiving transfers, card issuance, ATM withdrawals, or higher limits.
- When increasing limits, adding certain payment methods, or making international/cross‑border transfers.
- If activity changes (new device/country) or risk triggers require re‑verification.

What we check
- Document authenticity: Government‑issued ID (passport, driver’s license, national ID; residency permit where supported).
- Liveness/selfie: Confirms the person presenting the ID is you.
- Data consistency: Name, date of birth, and address may be matched; proof of address can be requested.
- Screening: Sanctions and politically exposed person (PEP) lists, per regulations.

Benefits to you
- Stronger account protection and faster support resolution.
- Access to more features and higher funding/transfer limits.
- Smoother payments with fewer compliance holds.

If you don’t verify
- Features remain limited (e.g., restricted transfers, lower limits, card issuance blocked).
- Activity may be paused or reviewed until verification is complete.

Privacy & security
- Your verification data is encrypted and used only for compliance and security. Access is restricted and retention follows legal requirements.

Frequency & timing
- Usually a one‑time process completed in minutes; manual reviews may take up to 24–48 hours. Re‑verification can be requested if details change or risk rules require it.
